judgments.evidence: Submission 2 is tighter and better laid out. The name input sits inline with Add person on desktop, amount and payer share a row, and balances read as a compact 'Ana is owed … $46.66' line, so the whole trip fits with clearer scanning. Submission 1 is equally on-brand but looser: a full-width Paid by select, bordered checkbox chips, two-line balance rows, and on mobile the expense amount is pushed below the details beside Remove, which costs a lot of vertical space.

Submission 2 is equally on-brand but less informative, and its tagline is indented under the wordmark text rather than aligned with the rule, so the header looks slightly less tidy.

Submission 2 separates the add-expense form from the expense list with its own section headings. Its Remove buttons sit neatly on the right, and the bolder right-aligned amounts give a clearer hierarchy at both widths. Submission 1 runs the form and list together in one long panel and stacks a Remove button under every item, though it does helpfully show per-person shares such as Ana ($3.34). Both follow the brand palette, wordmark and voice closely, so the cleaner structure of 2 tips it.
